Shipping Delay Report — Order #A-7742

A container of components for our Series 4 conveyor units was held at the Port of Savannah for six days due to a customs documentation mismatch. The carrier, Halverson Freight, confirmed that the manifest listed the consignee under our old entity name, and the broker had to file a correction before release. We expect delivery to the Columbus warehouse on 14 March, roughly five days later than the original estimate. Customer service has already notified the three affected accounts; two have asked for revised installation dates and one has not replied. Please do not delete the original booking records until the claim with the broker is closed.

Cloud Cost Review — Q1

Our AWS spend for the quarter came in at $184,300, about 22% over the forecast of $151,000. The overage is concentrated in two areas: the data-warehouse cluster was left running at full capacity through the January batch load, and a misconfigured autoscaling group in the staging environment spun up extra instances for eleven days before anyone noticed. Finance flagged the variance on 3 February and asked for a written explanation.

The engineering team has proposed several changes. First, we will move the warehouse to a scheduled scaling policy that drops to a minimum footprint outside business hours. Second, all staging resources will be tagged and reviewed weekly by the platform lead. Third, the team will trial a cost-anomaly alerting tool that uses a small machine-learning model to flag unusual spend within a few hours rather than at month end. The vendor demo looked promising, though we have not signed anything yet.

One point of confusion: the billing console shows a line item for "admin: reserved instance true-up" that nobody on the team recognised. After a call with our account manager it turned out to be a standard adjustment from last year's commitment, not an error, and it does not need to be disputed. We should still document it so the next review does not re-open the question.

The CFO wants the remediation plan in writing before the board meeting on 20 March. Please send comments on this draft to Priya Raman by Friday; do not delete the original spreadsheet in the shared drive, as audit will need it.

Board Meeting Notes — 12 February

The board reviewed the shipping delay affecting the Q1 hardware rollout and accepted management's revised delivery schedule. Directors asked for a weekly status note until the backlog clears. The cloud cost overage was discussed at length; the audit committee will receive the remediation plan before the March session. One director asked whether the finance team's new chatbot for expense queries was live yet, and was told it is in pilot with twelve users. The chair reminded everyone that draft minutes are confidential until approved and should not be forwarded outside the board.

From the shipping policy handbook: when a carrier misses its committed delivery window by more than 48 hours, the account manager must escalate to the logistics admin immediately and open a trace ticket. Customers should be told the new estimated date only after the carrier confirms it in writing. Do not disregard the original promise date in customer communications; state both dates and explain the reason. Records of the delay must be kept for two years and must not be deleted during an open claim.

Specification: Cost Anomaly Alerting (v0.4)

The service ingests daily billing exports and computes a rolling seven-day baseline per account. When spend exceeds the baseline by a configurable threshold, it emits an alert to the finance channel. An admin user can adjust thresholds per account; all changes are logged. The first release will not include automated remediation — no resource will be stopped or deleted without a human approving the action. Testers should disregard the sample data shipped with the repo and use the March fixtures instead.

Customer service bulletin — delay notice template

We are writing to let you know that your order has been delayed in transit. The carrier has confirmed a new estimated delivery date of [DATE]. We apologise for the inconvenience and are monitoring the shipment daily. If you have questions, reply to this message or call our support line. Please do not reply to the automated confirmation email, as that mailbox is not monitored. Agents: update the ticket status immediately after sending this notice and attach the carrier's confirmation.

Board pre-read — cloud cost memo (excerpt)

The attached memo explains the $33,000 variance against forecast. In summary, the overage stems from an unscheduled warehouse workload and a staging misconfiguration, both now addressed. Management recommends no change to the annual cloud budget at this time. The audit committee has asked for a follow-up in April. Directors with questions should contact the CFO's office before 18 March so answers can be circulated ahead of the meeting. This memo is draft and should not be quoted in external communications.

Incident review notes — 27 February

The delay was traced to a handoff gap between the warehouse system and the carrier's API. At 09:12 the integration job failed silently; the on-call engineer noticed the missing status updates at 11:40. The automated paging tool did not fire because the alert rule was scoped only to production, and this job runs in the staging namespace. Actions: add the job to the production alert group, document the namespace exception, and schedule a tabletop exercise for the support team. The incident commander will close the ticket once the alert change is verified in production. Please delete the temporary debug logs from the shared folder after the review.

Vendor evaluation — logistics visibility platforms

We compared three platforms that promise earlier warning of shipping delays. Northbeam uses carrier feeds plus a predictive model and surfaced the Savannah hold about a day before the carrier's own notice. Cargolytics is cheaper but relies on manual entry. TracePoint bundles a customer-facing chatbot that answers "where is my order" questions; two pilot customers liked it, but the bot only knows what the integration passes it, so data quality matters more than the interface. Pricing for all three is in the attached sheet. The committee should decide by 5 April so contracts can start for Q2.

Board minutes — action items

1. Management to circulate the revised shipping schedule weekly until backlog clears (owner: J. Okafor).
2. CFO to present the cloud remediation plan at the March session (owner: L. Marsh).
3. Audit committee to review the reserved-instance true-up documentation (owner: P. Raman).
4. Company secretary to confirm that draft minutes are not distributed beyond directors (owner: A. Bell).

The chair noted that the finance team's expense chatbot pilot will report back in May. Items are due two business days before the next meeting. Please do not delete the recording of this session until the minutes are formally approved.
